references.text: Abraham offered food to the angels who visited him, just as Manoah wanted to hold back the angel and offer him food.
Instructions about a burnt offering to the Lord, which the angel refers to when he says that Manoah may offer a burnt offering to the Lord.
Gideon's meeting with the angel of the Lord has similar features - he did not recognize it was the angel of the Lord until later.
The continuation of the story where Manoah finally understands that it was the angel of the Lord.
Jacob wrestled with a heavenly figure and did not immediately understand who he was, similar to Manoah's lack of recognition.
The exhortation to show hospitality, for some have unknowingly had angels as guests - relevant to Manoah's situation.
